name: SaaS app
h1: Privacy policy for SaaS and web apps
metaTitle: SaaS Privacy Policy — GDPR Art. 13 Contents, Subprocessors, Cookies | PrivacyPage
metaDescription: What a SaaS or web app privacy policy needs: GDPR Article 13 information, subprocessors, cookies and analytics. Pair it with Terms of Service and a Cookie Policy.
answer: A SaaS or web app that collects account data needs a privacy policy. For EU users, GDPR Article 13 lists what to tell people when you collect their data: who you are and how to contact you, the purposes and legal basis, recipients such as subprocessors, how long you keep data, and their rights.

storeRule.title: Article 13 — Information to be provided
storeRule.quote: the identity and the contact details of the controller and, where applicable, of the controller’s representative

additionalRules.title: Purposes and legal basis
additionalRules.text: Article 13 also requires “the purposes of the processing for which the personal data are intended as well as the legal basis for the processing”.

additionalRules.title: Retention
additionalRules.text: State “the period for which the personal data will be stored, or if that is not possible, the criteria used to determine that period”.

additionalRules.title: Analytics disclosure
additionalRules.text: If you use Google Analytics, its terms say “You must disclose the use of Google Analytics, and how it collects and processes data.”

sdks.name: Stripe (payments)
dataCollected: Payment and transaction data Stripe receives as a processor for your business (Stripe calls your customers End Customers)

whereToPaste: Site footer on every page, and on sign-up and checkout screens.
Link it from your Terms of Service and Cookie Policy.

sampleClause.heading: Subprocessors
sampleClause.text: We use trusted service providers (subprocessors) to run the service: our cloud host stores your account data, Stripe processes payments, and our email provider sends account emails. They process data only on our instructions. The current list is at /subprocessors.

faqs.q: Does a SaaS need a privacy policy and terms?
faqs.a: A privacy policy explains data handling; Terms of Service set the rules of use. Most SaaS products publish both, and many add a Cookie Policy.
A third-party service that processes personal data on your behalf, such as hosting, email or payments. GDPR Article 13 asks you to name recipients or categories of recipients.
